questions.q: What is the naming convention for Oracle Fusion Cloud's quarterly releases?
options: The last two digits of the year plus a letter A through D for the quarter, such as 26A or 26C
Version numbers like 1.0, 2.0, 3.0
Random codenames chosen each quarter
The customer's own internal project name
questions.explain: Releases are named with the last two digits of the calendar year plus A, B, C, or D for which quarter it is — for example, 26A is the first release of 2026.

questions.q: How many quarterly updates does Oracle Fusion Cloud receive per year?
options: One, at the start of the fiscal year
Four
Two, every six months
It varies randomly by customer
questions.explain: Oracle ships four quarterly updates a year, keeping every customer on a recent version without a multi-year upgrade project.

questions.q: What is a 'cohort' in the context of Oracle Fusion Cloud updates?
options: A group of employees trained together during onboarding
A team of Oracle developers who write the update
A grouping (A, B, or C) that determines which month within the quarter a customer's environments are updated
A set of customers who all share one Oracle Fusion login
questions.explain: Cohorts stagger the rollout across different months within each quarter, giving Oracle a gradual release and customers a predictable schedule.

questions.q: Within a customer's own environments, which one is updated first?
options: Production, since it's the most important
Whichever environment the consultant logs into first
They are always updated at the exact same moment
Non-production (test), typically a few weeks before production
questions.explain: Non-production is updated first, giving the functional team time to review and test the changes before the same update reaches production.

questions.q: What does it mean for a new quarterly feature to be 'opt-in'?
options: It ships available but switched off, until the customer deliberately enables it
It is automatically turned on for every customer the moment the update lands
It is removed permanently from the system
It only works for customers in Cohort A
questions.explain: Opt-in features are shipped turned off by default, protecting customers from an update unexpectedly changing how their business runs until they deliberately enable the feature.
